sentences.en: When we got off work, my colleague and I walked to the company entrance together.
We both stood at the door — I looked at him, he looked at me, and neither of us went in first.
Finally I said: "After you, I'm not in a hurry."
My colleague said thanks and went in first.
The next morning, my colleague and I arrived at the company entrance together again.
My colleague looked at me and said: "After you."
I went in first, with my colleague right behind me.

quiz.q: What happens when the narrator and his colleague reach the door at the same time?
a: They argue about who is late

quiz.q: What does the narrator say to let his colleague go first?

a: The colleague says 你先 to the narrator

grammar.e: 你先 politely lets someone go, take, or do something ahead of you — a small, everyday courtesy.
grammar.x: 你先，我不着急。— After you, I'm not in a hurry.

grammar.e: 谁也不 + verb stresses that not a single person acts — everyone is holding back at the same time.
grammar.x: 谁也不先进去。— Neither of us went in first.

grammar.p: 你 V, 我 V (mirrored actions)
grammar.e: Repeating the same verb with 你 and 我 in turn shows two people doing the same thing back and forth, often out of hesitation.
grammar.x: 你看看我，我看看你。— I looked at him, he looked at me.
